calls.reason: The Register confirms Anthropic moved enterprise customers to usage billing, but nothing shows cancellations or commercial decline. Anthropic's May notice of higher usage limits cuts against a simple story of subsidies being withdrawn.
OpenAI's Q1 operating loss and 39% gross margin are reported without a training-cost breakdown. The Anthropic estimate is for 2025, so Q1 profit without training can't be worked out.
OpenAI's reported Q1 cash burn and Anthropic's net losses point one way. Anthropic's filed Q2 operating profit points the other, so the evidence on whether the business models work is mixed.
The papers support hallucinations being unavoidable in theory, and Meta's spending caps show some customer pushback. Nothing ties these to higher bills or to negative margins for OpenAI or Anthropic.

Independent studies found many fully accurate, grounded AI research answers: all five models got a clinical question right, and Lexis+ AI was accurate 65% of the time. That undercuts the claim that every answer has hallucinations.

Epoch's measured cost declines and Anthropic's price cuts undercut the 'not getting cheaper' line. The main forecasts, about data centers, profitability and funding, have no deadline and remain unresolved.
